## Data sources

This analysis uses public-use data from the **National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)**, August 2021–August 2023 cycle. NHANES is a cross-sectional survey of the civilian non-institutionalised U.S. population that combines a household interview with a standardised physical examination and laboratory tests performed in a mobile examination centre (MEC).

Data are released as separate component files linked by the unique participant identifier `SEQN`. The files required for the present study are:

- **DEMO_L** — demographic variables (age, sex, race/ethnicity), interview and examination status, and the survey design variables (masked variance stratum `SDMVSTRA` and primary sampling unit `SDMVPSU`).
- **ALB_CR_L** — urine albumin and creatinine concentrations and the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (`URDACT`, mg/g). This ratio supplies the binary primary outcome (elevated albuminuria: ACR ≥ 30 mg/g).
- **BIOPRO_L** — standard biochemistry profile, including serum creatinine (`LBXSCR`). Serum creatinine is required to calculate estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation. This file also contains the phlebotomy sample weight.
- **GHB_L** — glycated haemoglobin (`LBXGH`, %). Used as one component of the diabetes definition.
- **BMX_L** — body measures, including body mass index (`BMXBMI`, kg/m²).
- **BPXO_L** — oscillometric blood-pressure readings obtained in the MEC.
- **DIQ_L** — diabetes questionnaire (self-reported diagnosis, insulin use, and oral agents).
- **BPQ_L** — blood-pressure questionnaire (self-reported hypertension and antihypertensive medication).
- **SMQ_L** — cigarette-smoking questionnaire.

Because eGFR and the diabetes definition rely on blood laboratory measures, the appropriate survey weight is the phlebotomy 2-year weight (`WTPH2YR`). This weight adjusts for the fact that not every examined participant provided a blood sample. It is used together with the design variables `SDMVSTRA` and `SDMVPSU` from the demographics file. Interview and MEC examination weights are retained for descriptive checks but are not the primary analytic weights. No weighted estimates are calculated at this stage.

All files were obtained from the CDC NHANES public-use repository for the August 2021–August 2023 cycle.


```{r download-raw-datasets, include=FALSE}
dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

files <- c(
  "DEMO_L.XPT",
  "ALB_CR_L.XPT",
  "BIOPRO_L.XPT",
  "GHB_L.XPT",
  "BMX_L.XPT",
  "BPXO_L.XPT",
  "DIQ_L.XPT",
  "BPQ_L.XPT",
  "SMQ_L.XPT"
)

base_url <- "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2021/DataFiles/"

for (f in files) {
  dest <- file.path("data/raw", f)
  if (!file.exists(dest)) {
    download.file(
      url = paste0(base_url, f),
      destfile = dest,
      mode = "wb"
    )
    message("Downloaded: ", f)
  } else {
    message("Already present: ", f)
  }
}

list.files("data/raw")
```

```{r load-raw-datasets, include=FALSE}
demo  <- read_xpt("data/raw/DEMO_L.XPT")
alb   <- read_xpt("data/raw/ALB_CR_L.XPT")
bio   <- read_xpt("data/raw/BIOPRO_L.XPT")
ghb   <- read_xpt("data/raw/GHB_L.XPT")
bmx   <- read_xpt("data/raw/BMX_L.XPT")
bpxo  <- read_xpt("data/raw/BPXO_L.XPT")
diq   <- read_xpt("data/raw/DIQ_L.XPT")
bpq   <- read_xpt("data/raw/BPQ_L.XPT")
smq   <- read_xpt("data/raw/SMQ_L.XPT")

tibble(
  file   = c("DEMO_L", "ALB_CR_L", "BIOPRO_L", "GHB_L", "BMX_L",
             "BPXO_L", "DIQ_L", "BPQ_L", "SMQ_L"),
  n_rows = c(nrow(demo), nrow(alb), nrow(bio), nrow(ghb), nrow(bmx),
             nrow(bpxo), nrow(diq), nrow(bpq), nrow(smq)),
  n_cols = c(ncol(demo), ncol(alb), ncol(bio), ncol(ghb), ncol(bmx),
             ncol(bpxo), ncol(diq), ncol(bpq), ncol(smq))
)
```

## Source files and structure

The component files were read with `haven::read_xpt()`. Each selected file contains one row per participant and is linked by the common identifier `SEQN`. The table below records the number of rows and columns in each source file as released by CDC.

```{r source-files-structure}
file_summary <- tibble(
  file   = c("DEMO_L", "ALB_CR_L", "BIOPRO_L", "GHB_L", "BMX_L",
             "BPXO_L", "DIQ_L", "BPQ_L", "SMQ_L"),
  n_rows = c(nrow(demo), nrow(alb), nrow(bio), nrow(ghb), nrow(bmx),
             nrow(bpxo), nrow(diq), nrow(bpq), nrow(smq)),
  n_cols = c(ncol(demo), ncol(alb), ncol(bio), ncol(ghb), ncol(bmx),
             ncol(bpxo), ncol(diq), ncol(bpq), ncol(smq))
)

knitr::kable(
  file_summary,
  col.names = c("File", "Rows", "Columns"),
  caption = "Dimensions of the NHANES August 2021–August 2023 source files used in this analysis"
)
```

## Primary outcome source: urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio

Elevated albuminuria is defined from the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. In the `ALB_CR_L` file this ratio is stored in the variable `URDACT` (mg/g). The table below summarises the observed values and the extent of missingness in the source file.

```{r inspect-acr}
acr_summary <- tibble(
  `Records in component` = nrow(alb),
  `ACR available` = sum(!is.na(alb$URDACT)),
  `ACR missing` = sum(is.na(alb$URDACT)),
  `Available (%)` = round(100 * mean(!is.na(alb$URDACT)), 1),
  `Median ACR (mg/g)` = round(median(alb$URDACT, na.rm=TRUE), 2),
  `ACR >=30 mg/g (n)` = sum(alb$URDACT >= 30, na.rm=TRUE)
)
knitr::kable(acr_summary, caption="Urinary ACR availability and distribution within ALB_CR_L")
```

This is a source-component summary, not an estimate of albuminuria prevalence in the eligible study population. Missing measurements and the overlap with other required components are assessed separately below.

## Key laboratory measures: serum creatinine and HbA1c

Serum creatinine (`LBXSCR` in `BIOPRO_L`) is required to calculate eGFR with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation. Glycated haemoglobin (`LBXGH` in `GHB_L`) contributes to the diabetes definition. Both files contain the phlebotomy weight `WTPH2YR`. The summaries below show the observed ranges and missingness in the source files.

```{r inspect-creatinine-hba1c}
lab_summary <- tibble(
  Measurement=c("Serum creatinine (mg/dL)", "HbA1c (%)"),
  `Source records`=c(nrow(bio),nrow(ghb)),
  `Available (n)`=c(sum(!is.na(bio$LBXSCR)),sum(!is.na(ghb$LBXGH))),
  `Missing (n)`=c(sum(is.na(bio$LBXSCR)),sum(is.na(ghb$LBXGH))),
  Median=c(median(bio$LBXSCR,na.rm=TRUE),median(ghb$LBXGH,na.rm=TRUE))
)
knitr::kable(lab_summary,digits=2,caption="Availability of blood laboratory measures within their respective source components")
```

A participant can have a laboratory-component record but no reported result. The source counts do not establish the reason for each missing result.

## Body mass index

Body mass index is obtained from the body-measures examination file (`BMX_L`). The variable `BMXBMI` is expressed in kg/m² and will be used both as a continuous covariate and to identify obesity (BMI ≥ 30) as one of the metabolic risk factors.

```{r inspect-bmi}
bmi_summary <- tibble(
  `Source records`=nrow(bmx),
  `BMI available`=sum(!is.na(bmx$BMXBMI)),
  `BMI missing`=sum(is.na(bmx$BMXBMI)),
  `Median BMI (kg/m²)`=round(median(bmx$BMXBMI,na.rm=TRUE),1)
)
knitr::kable(bmi_summary,caption="BMI availability within BMX_L")
```

These summaries are calculated on the full body-measures file and include participants younger than 20 years.

## Blood-pressure examination

Oscillometric blood-pressure readings are stored in `BPXO_L`. The file contains up to three systolic (`BPXOSY1`–`BPXOSY3`) and diastolic (`BPXODI1`–`BPXODI3`) measurements. These readings will be used, together with questionnaire data, to define hypertension.

```{r inspect-bp}
bp_summary <- tibble(
  Reading=c("Systolic 1","Systolic 2","Systolic 3",
            "Diastolic 1","Diastolic 2","Diastolic 3"),
  `Available (n)`=vapply(bpxo[c("BPXOSY1","BPXOSY2","BPXOSY3",
                               "BPXODI1","BPXODI2","BPXODI3")],
                         function(x) sum(!is.na(x)),numeric(1))
)
knitr::kable(bp_summary,caption="Availability of repeated oscillometric blood-pressure readings")
```

The readings are assessed individually here. Rules for calculating mean blood pressure will be documented when variables are derived.

## Diabetes questionnaire

The diabetes questionnaire (`DIQ_L`) records whether a participant has ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that they have diabetes, and whether they are currently using insulin or oral diabetes medication.

- `DIQ010` asks: “Has a doctor or other health professional ever told you that you have diabetes?” (1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = borderline).
- `DIQ050` asks whether the participant is now taking insulin.
- `DIQ070` asks whether the participant is now taking diabetic pills to lower blood sugar.

These self-reported items will later be used, together with the laboratory measure of glycated haemoglobin, to identify participants who have diabetes. The precise rule for combining the questionnaire answers with the laboratory result will be specified when the analysis variables are created. Here we only confirm that the source variables exist and examine their basic distributions.

```{r inspect-dm}
questionnaire_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("DIQ010","DIQ050","DIQ070"), function(v) {
  x <- diq[[v]]
  tab <- table(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA (not recorded / not applicable)", as.character(x)))
  tibble(Variable=v, `Response code`=names(tab), N=as.integer(tab))
}))
knitr::kable(questionnaire_counts, caption="Diabetes questionnaire response codes")
```

Questionnaire codes are reported without recoding. Missing entries on follow-up items may reflect the survey's routing rules; their interpretation will be checked against the relevant questionnaire documentation before phenotype construction.

## Blood-pressure questionnaire

The blood-pressure questionnaire (`BPQ_L`) records whether a participant has ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that they have hypertension (high blood pressure), and whether they are currently taking medication for it.

- `BPQ020` asks: “Have you ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?”
- `BPQ030` asks whether the participant was told this on two or more different visits.
- `BPQ150` asks whether the participant is now taking prescribed medicine for high blood pressure.

These self-reported answers will later be used, together with the blood-pressure readings taken during the physical examination, to identify participants who have hypertension. The exact rule for combining the questionnaire with the examination measurements will be set out when the study population is defined; here we only confirm that the source variables are present and examine their basic distributions.

```{r bp-quiestionare}
questionnaire_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("BPQ020","BPQ030","BPQ150"), function(v) {
  x <- bpq[[v]]
  tab <- table(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA (not recorded / not applicable)", as.character(x)))
  tibble(Variable=v, `Response code`=names(tab), N=as.integer(tab))
}))
knitr::kable(questionnaire_counts, caption="Blood-pressure questionnaire response codes")
```

Questionnaire codes are reported without recoding. Missing entries on follow-up items may reflect the survey's routing rules; their interpretation will be checked against the relevant questionnaire documentation before phenotype construction.

## Smoking questionnaire

Cigarette smoking status is taken from the smoking questionnaire (`SMQ_L`).

- `SMQ020` asks whether the participant has smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their entire life.
- `SMQ040` asks whether the participant now smokes cigarettes every day, some days, or not at all.

These two items are the standard source for classifying participants as never, former or current smokers. The classification rule itself will be applied when the analysis variables are created; here we only confirm that the source items are present and examine their distributions.

```{r smoking-questionare}
questionnaire_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("SMQ020","SMQ040"), function(v) {
  x <- smq[[v]]
  tab <- table(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA (not recorded / not applicable)", as.character(x)))
  tibble(Variable=v, `Response code`=names(tab), N=as.integer(tab))
}))
knitr::kable(questionnaire_counts, caption="Smoking questionnaire response codes")
```

Questionnaire codes are reported without recoding. Missing entries on follow-up items may reflect the survey's routing rules; their interpretation will be checked against the relevant questionnaire documentation before phenotype construction.

## Missingness of key source variables

The table below shows the number and percentage of missing values for the main variables that will be used to define the outcome, the metabolic risk factors and the covariates. Percentages are calculated from the total number of records in each source file. These percentages use the number of records within each respective component as the denominator. They do not count participants absent from the component altogether. Follow-up questionnaire items may be intentionally skipped.

```{r missingness-vars}
missing_summary <- tibble(
  Variable = c(
    "Urine ACR (URDACT)",
    "Serum creatinine (LBXSCR)",
    "HbA1c (LBXGH)",
    "BMI (BMXBMI)",
    "Systolic BP (BPXOSY1)",
    "Age (RIDAGEYR)",
    "Sex (RIAGENDR)",
    "Race/ethnicity (RIDRETH3)",
    "Diabetes self-report (DIQ010)",
    "Insulin use (DIQ050)",
    "Oral diabetes medication (DIQ070)",
    "Hypertension self-report (BPQ020)",
    "Antihypertensive medication (BPQ150)",
    "Smoking 100+ cigarettes (SMQ020)"
  ),
  Source_file = c(
    "ALB_CR_L", "BIOPRO_L", "GHB_L", "BMX_L", "BPXO_L",
    "DEMO_L", "DEMO_L", "DEMO_L",
    "DIQ_L", "DIQ_L", "DIQ_L",
    "BPQ_L", "BPQ_L", "SMQ_L"
  ),
  N_missing = c(
    sum(is.na(alb$URDACT)),
    sum(is.na(bio$LBXSCR)),
    sum(is.na(ghb$LBXGH)),
    sum(is.na(bmx$BMXBMI)),
    sum(is.na(bpxo$BPXOSY1)),
    sum(is.na(demo$RIDAGEYR)),
    sum(is.na(demo$RIAGENDR)),
    sum(is.na(demo$RIDRETH3)),
    sum(is.na(diq$DIQ010)),
    sum(is.na(diq$DIQ050)),
    sum(is.na(diq$DIQ070)),
    sum(is.na(bpq$BPQ020)),
    sum(is.na(bpq$BPQ150)),
    sum(is.na(smq$SMQ020))
  ),
  N_total = c(
    nrow(alb), nrow(bio), nrow(ghb), nrow(bmx), nrow(bpxo),
    nrow(demo), nrow(demo), nrow(demo),
    nrow(diq), nrow(diq), nrow(diq),
    nrow(bpq), nrow(bpq), nrow(smq)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Pct_missing = round(100 * N_missing / N_total, 1))

knitr::kable(
  missing_summary,
  col.names = c("Variable", "Source file", "Missing (n)", "Total (n)", "Missing (%)"),
  caption = "Missingness of key source variables required for the research question"
)
```
Age, sex and race/ethnicity have no missing values in the demographics source. The laboratory files contain records with missing measurements: these must be distinguished from participants who have no record in the component. The observed source-level missingness does not, by itself, establish whether a missing laboratory result was due to eligibility, specimen collection, processing or another reason.

Missing values on conditional questionnaire items (including diabetes and blood-pressure medication questions) can arise from planned skip patterns. They should not automatically be classified as nonresponse; equally, each missing entry should not be assumed to be a confirmed skip without consulting the questionnaire routing rules.

## Range and consistency checks

The distributions of key continuous variables were assessed using observed minimum, median and maximum values. These descriptive summaries were reviewed for potentially implausible or extreme measurements in clinical context. No formal out-of-range count was calculated, and no records were modified or excluded during this assessment.

```{r range-check}
range_checks <- tibble(
  Variable = c("Urine ACR (mg/g)", "Serum creatinine (mg/dL)", "HbA1c (%)",
               "BMI (kg/m²)", "Systolic BP (mmHg)"),
  Min = c(
    min(alb$URDACT, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(bio$LBXSCR, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(ghb$LBXGH, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(bmx$BMXBMI, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(bpxo$BPXOSY1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Median = c(
    median(alb$URDACT, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(bio$LBXSCR, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(ghb$LBXGH, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(bmx$BMXBMI, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(bpxo$BPXOSY1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Max = c(
    max(alb$URDACT, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(bio$LBXSCR, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(ghb$LBXGH, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(bmx$BMXBMI, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(bpxo$BPXOSY1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  range_checks,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Variable", "Minimum", "Median", "Maximum"),
  caption = "Observed ranges of key continuous variables"
)
```
The highest values observed are large but remain within ranges reported in clinical populations (ACR values above 5 000 mg/g can occur in the nephrotic range; creatinine values above 5 mg/dL and systolic readings above 200 mmHg are uncommon but physiologically possible). No records are removed during the source-data assessment.

## Component linkage and measurement availability

NHANES components can be linked through the participant identifier `SEQN`. Before defining any study eligibility criteria, we assessed whether records in each selected component have a matching demographic record, and how many linked records belong to adults aged 20 years or older. This is a source-data linkage assessment, **not** a participant eligibility flow.

```{r linkage-assessment}
components <- list(
  DEMO_L=demo, ALB_CR_L=alb, BIOPRO_L=bio, GHB_L=ghb,
  BMX_L=bmx, BPXO_L=bpxo, DIQ_L=diq, BPQ_L=bpq, SMQ_L=smq
)
linkage_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(components), function(component) {
  x <- components[[component]]
  matched <- x$SEQN %in% demo$SEQN
  adults <- x$SEQN %in% demo$SEQN[!is.na(demo$RIDAGEYR) & demo$RIDAGEYR >= 20]
  tibble(
    Component=component,
    `Source records`=nrow(x),
    `Unique SEQN`=dplyr::n_distinct(x$SEQN),
    `N linked to demographics`=sum(matched),
    `Matched adults (age >=20)`=sum(adults)
  )
}))
knitr::kable(
  linkage_summary,
  caption = "Record linkage to demographics and adult coverage by source component. Counts in the linkage column show the number of records whose participant identifier (SEQN) was found in the demographics file."
)
```


Because ACR and serum creatinine are essential to the proposed research question, we also assessed their **joint availability among adults**, rather than only their separate component-level missingness.

```{r joint-availability}
availability <- demo %>%
  filter(!is.na(RIDAGEYR), RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  select(SEQN) %>%
  left_join(alb %>% select(SEQN, URDACT), by="SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bio %>% select(SEQN, LBXSCR), by="SEQN")
availability_summary <- tibble(
  Assessment=c("Adults in demographics",
               "Adults with ACR measured",
               "Adults with serum creatinine measured",
               "Adults with both ACR and serum creatinine measured"),
  N=c(nrow(availability),
      sum(!is.na(availability$URDACT)),
      sum(!is.na(availability$LBXSCR)),
      sum(!is.na(availability$URDACT) & !is.na(availability$LBXSCR)))
)
knitr::kable(availability_summary,
  caption="Joint availability of the two essential kidney measurements among adults")
```

These counts describe the feasibility of linking required measurements. They do not apply eGFR thresholds, metabolic risk criteria or other eligibility rules. The participant inclusion/exclusion flow will be produced during ARD construction.

## Summary of source-data assessment

The selected NHANES August 2021–August 2023 files provide source variables for urinary ACR, serum creatinine, HbA1c, BMI, repeated blood-pressure readings, relevant questionnaire responses, demographics and survey design. The component-level summaries above describe measurement availability, observed ranges and response coding; the linkage assessment examines coverage across files.

Missing values on the medication items are structural: the questions are asked only after a positive answer to the diagnosis item. Missingness on serum creatinine and HbA1c reflects participants who did not provide a blood sample. Observed ranges for the continuous measures are physiologically plausible. No records were excluded during this source-data assessment.

The source files are suitable for constructing the study population and analysis variables. Subsequent work will apply the eligibility criteria, define the derived variables and document the inclusion flow.


### Data integration and participant linkage

The nine NHANES component files were linked on the unique participant identifier (SEQN). The demographic file (DEMO_L) served as the reference population. Selected variables from the urine albumin–creatinine, biochemistry, glycated haemoglobin, body-measures, blood-pressure examination, diabetes questionnaire, blood-pressure questionnaire and smoking questionnaire files were joined to the demographic file by left join, so that every interviewed participant was retained at this stage. Each source file contained a unique SEQN and the joins preserved both the original number of demographic records and the uniqueness of SEQN.

```{r merge-nhanes-component}
# Confirm uniqueness of SEQN in each source file before joining
source_files <- list(
  DEMO_L = demo, ALB_CR_L = alb, BIOPRO_L = bio, GHB_L = ghb,
  BMX_L = bmx, BPXO_L = bpxo, DIQ_L = diq, BPQ_L = bpq, SMQ_L = smq
)

uniqueness_check <- bind_rows(lapply(names(source_files), function(nm) {
  x <- source_files[[nm]]
  tibble(
    File = nm,
    Rows = nrow(x),
    Unique_SEQN = n_distinct(x$SEQN),
    Duplicates = sum(duplicated(x$SEQN))
  )
}))

# Merge, retaining only the variables required for subsequent derivation
ard <- demo %>%
  select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR, RIDRETH3, RIDEXPRG,
       SDMVSTRA, SDMVPSU, WTINT2YR, WTMEC2YR) %>%
  left_join(alb  %>% select(SEQN, URDACT), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bio  %>% select(SEQN, LBXSCR, WTPH2YR), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(ghb  %>% select(SEQN, LBXGH), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bmx  %>% select(SEQN, BMXBMI), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bpxo %>% select(SEQN,
                            BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3,
                            BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(diq  %>% select(SEQN, DIQ010, DIQ050, DIQ070), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bpq  %>% select(SEQN, BPQ020, BPQ030, BPQ150), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(smq  %>% select(SEQN, SMQ020, SMQ040), by = "SEQN")

merge_check <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Rows in demographic file",
              "Rows after joins",
              "Unique SEQN after joins",
              "Duplicate SEQN after joins"),
  Value = c(nrow(demo),
            nrow(ard),
            n_distinct(ard$SEQN),
            sum(duplicated(ard$SEQN)))
)

knitr::kable(uniqueness_check,
             caption = "Participant uniqueness within each source file")
knitr::kable(merge_check,
             caption = "Row count and participant uniqueness after linkage")
```

After linkage the combined dataset contained 11 933 records and 11 933 unique participant identifiers, with no duplicates. The unchanged row count confirmed that no unintended record multiplication occurred. Participant-level linkage integrity was therefore established, while incomplete availability of measurements and questionnaire items across components was retained for later evaluation.



#### Kidney function and albuminuria

Estimated glomerular filtration rate was calculated from serum creatinine (LBXSCR, mg/dL), age and sex using the CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation, which does not include a race coefficient:

\[
\text{eGFR} = 142 \times \min(\text{Scr}/\kappa, 1)^{\alpha} \times \max(\text{Scr}/\kappa, 1)^{-1.200} \times 0.9938^{\text{Age}} \times 1.012^{\text{[female]}}
\]

where Scr is serum creatinine in mg/dL, \(\kappa = 0.7\) (female) or \(0.9\) (male), and \(\alpha = -0.241\) (female) or \(-0.302\) (male). The equation was applied only to participants aged 20 years or older with non-missing serum creatinine and recorded sex; eGFR was set to missing otherwise. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (URDACT, mg/g) was retained as a continuous variable. Elevated albuminuria was defined as ACR ≥ 30 mg/g among participants with a non-missing ACR.


```{r derive-egfr}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    # CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation (adults only)
    kappa = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, 0.7, 0.9),
    alpha = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, -0.241, -0.302),
    female_factor = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, 1.012, 1),
    egfr = if_else(
      RIDAGEYR >= 20 &
        !is.na(LBXSCR) & LBXSCR > 0 &
        RIAGENDR %in% c(1, 2),
      142 *
        pmin(LBXSCR / kappa, 1)^alpha *
        pmax(LBXSCR / kappa, 1)^(-1.200) *
        0.9938^RIDAGEYR *
        female_factor,
      NA_real_
    ),
    # Elevated albuminuria
    elevated_acr = if_else(!is.na(URDACT), URDACT >= 30, NA)
  )

kidney_check <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adults         = n(),
    n_with_creatinine = sum(!is.na(LBXSCR)),
    n_with_egfr      = sum(!is.na(egfr)),
    egfr_min         = min(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    egfr_median      = median(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    egfr_max         = max(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_egfr_lt_60     = sum(egfr < 60, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_with_acr       = sum(!is.na(URDACT)),
    n_acr_ge_30      = sum(elevated_acr, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

knitr::kable(
  kidney_check,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Kidney function and albuminuria: availability and distribution after derivation"
)
```
Among 7 809 adults aged 20 years or older, serum creatinine was available for 5 443 participants, all of whom had sufficient information for calculation of eGFR. Median eGFR was 93.6 mL/min/1.73 m² (range 3.5–143.4), and 477 participants had eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Urine ACR was available for 5 910 adults, of whom 721 (12.2 %) had elevated albuminuria (ACR ≥ 30 mg/g). These figures describe measurement availability and kidney-related characteristics before application of the full study eligibility criteria.

#### Blood pressure

Blood pressure was assessed using the NHANES oscillometric examination protocol. Following five minutes of seated rest, up to three consecutive systolic and diastolic measurements were obtained approximately 60 seconds apart with an automated upper-arm device. Mean systolic and mean diastolic blood pressure were calculated separately from all available non-missing readings. The large majority of adults with blood-pressure data had all three readings; a small number had only one or two. The first reading was retained whenever it was present. Participants with no available readings for a given measure were assigned a missing mean value.
```{r derive-bp-measure}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    mean_sbp = rowMeans(
      pick(BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_dbp = rowMeans(
      pick(BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_sbp = if_else(is.nan(mean_sbp), NA_real_, mean_sbp),
    mean_dbp = if_else(is.nan(mean_dbp), NA_real_, mean_dbp)
  )

bp_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adults    = n(),
    n_with_sbp  = sum(!is.na(mean_sbp)),
    n_with_dbp  = sum(!is.na(mean_dbp)),
    sbp_min     = min(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    sbp_median  = median(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    sbp_max     = max(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_min     = min(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_median  = median(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_max     = max(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

knitr::kable(
  bp_summary,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Availability and distribution of mean blood-pressure measurements among adults"
)
```

```{r temp}
tibble(
  Readings = c("Three", "Two", "One"),
  N = c(5842, 15, 6)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Number of available blood-pressure readings among adults with a calculated mean")
```
Among 7,809 adults aged 20 years or older, mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure could be calculated for 5,863 participants (75.1 %). Median systolic blood pressure was 120.3 mmHg (range 70–232.3 mmHg) and median diastolic blood pressure was 74.0 mmHg (range 34–139 mmHg). The observed extremes are uncommon but remain physiologically possible; no values were excluded at this stage. Participants without valid measurements retained missing values rather than being assigned zero. These derived measurements will contribute to the hypertension definition and subsequent analyses. Of the 5,863 adults for whom mean blood pressure was calculated, 5,842 had three systolic and three diastolic measurements, 15 had two of each, and 6 had one of each.

#### Metabolic risk factors

Metabolic risk was defined using three non-mutually exclusive clinical phenotypes: diabetes, hypertension and obesity. These conditions identify adults with established metabolic risk factors associated with kidney disease, consistent with the study objective of examining albuminuria among individuals with preserved estimated kidney function.

Each phenotype was constructed from questionnaire responses, clinical measurements and, where applicable, medication-use information. Classification followed three rules:

- **Present** — at least one defining criterion was positive, even if other components were missing.  
- **Absent** — the available information met the phenotype-specific criteria for a negative classification, taking account of questionnaire skip patterns.  
- **Indeterminate** — neither presence nor absence could be established.

Overall metabolic risk was defined as the presence of at least one of the three phenotypes. This approach avoided treating incomplete information as evidence that a condition was absent.

##### Diabetes

Diabetes was classified as **present** if any of the following was true:

- self-reported physician diagnosis (DIQ010 = 1), **or**
- HbA1c ≥ 6.5 %, **or**
- current insulin use (DIQ050 = 1), **or**
- current use of diabetes pills (DIQ070 = 1).

Diabetes was classified as **absent** in either of the following situations:

- the participant reported no diagnosis (DIQ010 = 2) **and** HbA1c was measured and below 6.5 %, **or**
- the participant reported borderline diabetes (DIQ010 = 3), HbA1c was measured and below 6.5 %, **and** neither insulin nor diabetes pills were reported.

When a participant reported no diagnosis, the medication items were not asked; the resulting structural missingness was treated as non-informative. In all other cases diabetes status was left **indeterminate**.

```{r dm-derive}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    diabetes = case_when(
  # Present
  DIQ010 == 1 | LBXGH >= 6.5 | DIQ050 == 1 | DIQ070 == 1 ~ 1,

  # Absent: clear negative self-report + measured HbA1c < 6.5
  DIQ010 == 2 & !is.na(LBXGH) & LBXGH < 6.5 ~ 0,

  # Absent: borderline self-report, no diabetes medication, measured HbA1c < 6.5
  DIQ010 == 3 & !is.na(LBXGH) & LBXGH < 6.5 &
    (is.na(DIQ050) | DIQ050 != 1) &
    (is.na(DIQ070) | DIQ070 != 1) ~ 0,

  # Indeterminate
  TRUE ~ NA_real_
)
  )

diabetes_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(diabetes, name = "N") %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1),
    diabetes = case_when(
      diabetes == 1 ~ "Present",
      diabetes == 0 ~ "Absent",
      TRUE ~ "Indeterminate"
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  diabetes_summary,
  caption = "Diabetes phenotype among adults"
)
```

Among 7,809 adults aged 20 years or older, 1,312 (16.8 %) met the diabetes definition, 4,735 (60.6 %) were classified as not having diabetes, and 1,762 (22.6 %) had insufficient information for a definitive classification.


##### Hypertension

Hypertension was classified as **present** if any of the following was true:

- self-reported physician diagnosis (BPQ020 = 1), **or**
- current use of prescribed medication for high blood pressure (BPQ150 = 1), **or**
- mean systolic blood pressure ≥ 130 mmHg, **or**
- mean diastolic blood pressure ≥ 80 mmHg.

Hypertension was classified as **absent** only when both of the following held:

- the participant reported no previous diagnosis (BPQ020 = 2), **and**
- both mean systolic and mean diastolic blood pressure were measured and were below the thresholds above.

When a participant reported no diagnosis, the medication item was not asked; the resulting structural missingness was treated as non-informative. In all other cases hypertension status was left **indeterminate**.
The blood-pressure thresholds follow the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline definition of hypertension (≥130/80 mmHg).


```{r htn-derive}

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    hypertension = case_when(
      BPQ020 == 1 |
        BPQ150 == 1 |
        mean_sbp >= 130 |
        mean_dbp >= 80 ~ 1,

      BPQ020 == 2 &
        !is.na(mean_sbp) &
        !is.na(mean_dbp) &
        mean_sbp < 130 &
        mean_dbp < 80 ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

hypertension_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(hypertension, name = "N") %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1),
    hypertension = case_when(
      hypertension == 1 ~ "Present",
      hypertension == 0 ~ "Absent",
      TRUE ~ "Indeterminate"
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  hypertension_summary,
  caption = "Hypertension phenotype among adults"
)

```

Among 7809 adults aged 20 years or older, 4085 (52.3 %) met at least one criterion for hypertension and 2 489 (31.9 %) were classified as not having hypertension. Hypertension status remained indeterminate for 1235 participants (15.8 %) because the available information was insufficient to establish either presence or absence. These classifications were derived before application of the full study eligibility criteria.


##### Obesity

Obesity was classified as **present** if body mass index (BMI) was ≥ 30 kg/m² (BMXBMI).  

Obesity was classified as **absent** if BMI was measured and was below 30 kg/m².  

Participants without a valid BMI measurement were classified as **indeterminate**. BMI was also retained as a continuous variable for later analysis.


```{r obesity-derive}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    obesity = case_when(
      !is.na(BMXBMI) & BMXBMI >= 30 ~ 1,
      !is.na(BMXBMI) & BMXBMI < 30 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

obesity_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(obesity, name = "N") %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1),
    obesity = case_when(
      obesity == 1 ~ "Present",
      obesity == 0 ~ "Absent",
      TRUE ~ "Indeterminate"
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  obesity_summary,
  caption = "Obesity phenotype among adults"
)
```
Among 7,809 adults aged 20 years or older, 2,455 (31.4 %) met the BMI criterion for obesity and 3,515 (45.0 %) had BMI below 30 kg/m². Obesity status was indeterminate for 1,839 participants (23.5 %) because BMI measurements were unavailable. These classifications were derived before application of the full study eligibility criteria.

##### Combined metabolic risk

The three phenotypes were combined into a single indicator variable (`metabolic_risk`). As discussed earlier, a participant was classified as having metabolic risk if at least one phenotype was present. The indicator was absent only when all three phenotypes were absent, and indeterminate otherwise.


```{r metabolic-risk-derive}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    metabolic_risk = case_when(
      diabetes == 1 | hypertension == 1 | obesity == 1 ~ 1,
      diabetes == 0 & hypertension == 0 & obesity == 0 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

metabolic_risk_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(metabolic_risk, name = "N") %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1),
    metabolic_risk = case_when(
      metabolic_risk == 1 ~ "Present",
      metabolic_risk == 0 ~ "Absent",
      TRUE ~ "Indeterminate"
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  metabolic_risk_summary,
  caption = "Combined metabolic-risk classification among adults"
)
stopifnot(
  all(
    (ard$metabolic_risk == 1) ==
      (ard$diabetes == 1 | ard$hypertension == 1 | ard$obesity == 1),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
)
```
Among 7,809 adults aged 20 years or older, 5,021 (64.3 %) met at least one criterion for diabetes, hypertension or obesity. All three phenotypes were classified as absent in 1,576 participants (20.2 %), while metabolic-risk status remained indeterminate for 1,212 (15.5 %). These results describe metabolic-risk classification before application of the kidney-function and albuminuria eligibility criteria.

#### Demographic, laboratory and smoking variables

Age (years), sex and race/ethnicity were taken from the demographic file and retained in their original NHANES coding. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c, %), body mass index (BMI, kg/m²) and derived mean systolic blood pressure (mmHg) were retained as continuous covariates.

##### Smoking status

Smoking status was classified from self-reported lifetime and current cigarette use:

- **Never** — smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in lifetime (SMQ020 = 2).  
- **Former** — smoked at least 100 cigarettes (SMQ020 = 1) and now smokes not at all (SMQ040 = 3).  
- **Current** — smoked at least 100 cigarettes (SMQ020 = 1) and now smokes every day or some days (SMQ040 = 1 or 2).  

Participants with insufficient information were left unclassified (missing).


```{r smoking-derive}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    smoking_status = case_when(
      SMQ020 == 2 ~ "Never",
      SMQ020 == 1 & SMQ040 == 3 ~ "Former",
      SMQ020 == 1 & SMQ040 %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Current",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    smoking_status = factor(
      smoking_status,
      levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current")
    )
  )

smoking_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(smoking_status, name = "N", .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)
  )

knitr::kable(
  smoking_summary,
  caption = "Smoking status among adults"
)
```
Among 7,809 adults aged 20 years or older, 4,547 (58.2%) were classified as never smokers, 2,050 (26.3%) as former smokers and 1,183 (15.1%) as current smokers. Smoking status could not be determined for 29 participants (0.4%) because the available questionnaire responses were insufficient for classification. These figures describe the adult source population before application of the study eligibility criteria.

### Study population and eligibility criteria

The study population was drawn from participants in NHANES August 2021–August 2023.

Eligibility required all of the following:

- age ≥ 20 years,
- not currently pregnant,
- a valid urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and serum creatinine measurement,
- estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD-EPI 2021), and
- at least one metabolic risk factor (diabetes, hypertension or obesity).

Age ≥ 20 years was selected as the adult threshold, consistent with its use in major NHANES analyses of chronic kidney disease and metabolic risk factors (e.g., USRDS CKD surveillance reports; Wang et al., 2020). Pregnancy was excluded because physiological changes in kidney filtration and albumin excretion during pregnancy can alter the interpretation of both eGFR and ACR; the study objective concerns metabolic risk factors in non-pregnant adults.

Participants lacking the measurements required to establish kidney-function or albuminuria eligibility were excluded. Metabolic-risk eligibility required at least one positively identified phenotype; participants with no confirmed metabolic risk factor, including those with indeterminate overall metabolic-risk status, were not eligible. Missing values in covariates intended for later regression analysis did not constitute exclusion criteria.

Eligibility criteria were applied sequentially, and the number of participants remaining at each step was recorded to document cohort selection.

```{r eligibility-flag}
ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    eligible_age = !is.na(RIDAGEYR) & RIDAGEYR >= 20,
    eligible_not_pregnant = is.na(RIDEXPRG) | RIDEXPRG != 1,
    eligible_kidney_measurements = !is.na(URDACT) & !is.na(LBXSCR) & !is.na(egfr),
    eligible_egfr = !is.na(egfr) & egfr >= 60,
    eligible_metabolic_risk = !is.na(metabolic_risk) & metabolic_risk == 1,
    eligible_study = eligible_age &
                     eligible_not_pregnant &
                     eligible_kidney_measurements &
                     eligible_egfr &
                     eligible_metabolic_risk
  )

flow <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Demographic file",
    "Adults aged ≥ 20 years",
    "Not pregnant",
    "Valid ACR and serum creatinine",
    "eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²",
    "≥ 1 metabolic risk factor (final eligible population)"
  ),
  N = c(
    nrow(demo),
    sum(ard$eligible_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(ard$eligible_age & ard$eligible_not_pregnant, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(ard$eligible_age & ard$eligible_not_pregnant & ard$eligible_kidney_measurements, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(ard$eligible_age & ard$eligible_not_pregnant & ard$eligible_kidney_measurements & ard$eligible_egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(ard$eligible_study, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

stopifnot(
  all(diff(flow$N) <= 0),
  tail(flow$N, 1) == sum(ard$eligible_study),
  !anyNA(ard$eligible_study)
)

knitr::kable(
  flow,
  caption = "Participant selection flow"
)
```
Of the 11,933 participants in the demographic file, 7,809 were aged 20 years or older and 7,768 were not pregnant. Following sequential application of the kidney-measurement, eGFR and metabolic-risk eligibility criteria, 3,370 participants remained in the eligible study population.

```{r eligibility-event-summary}
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(ard$elevated_acr[ard$eligible_study])
)
ard %>%
  filter(eligible_study) %>%
  summarise(
    `Eligible participants` = n(),
    `Elevated albuminuria (ACR ≥ 30)` = sum(elevated_acr, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Eligible population and primary outcome events")
```


### Missing data

Missingness was assessed among the 3,370 participants who met the study eligibility criteria. The number and percentage of missing values were calculated for the primary outcome and the candidate regression covariates (age, sex, race/ethnicity, HbA1c, mean systolic blood pressure, BMI and smoking status).

Participants were not excluded from the analysis-ready dataset solely because of missing regression covariates. The extent of missingness was documented to inform the subsequent analytical approach.

```{r missingness-summary}
eligible <- ard %>%
  filter(eligible_study)

missingness <- tibble(
  Variable = c(
    "Elevated albuminuria",
    "Age",
    "Sex",
    "Race/ethnicity",
    "HbA1c",
    "Mean systolic blood pressure",
    "BMI",
    "Smoking status"
  ),
  Missing_N = c(
    sum(is.na(eligible$elevated_acr)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$RIDAGEYR)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$RIAGENDR)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$RIDRETH3)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$LBXGH)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$mean_sbp)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$BMXBMI)),
    sum(is.na(eligible$smoking_status))
  ),
  Total_N = nrow(eligible)
) %>%
  mutate(Missing_pct = round(100 * Missing_N / Total_N, 1))

knitr::kable(
  missingness,
  caption = "Missing data among eligible participants"
)
```
Among the 3,370 eligible participants, the primary outcome, age, sex, race/ethnicity and HbA1c were complete. Missingness was highest for mean systolic blood pressure (75 participants; 2.2 %), followed by BMI (23; 0.7 %) and smoking status (6; 0.2 %). Overall, missingness among the candidate regression covariates was low. All eligible participants were retained in the analysis-ready dataset regardless of covariate completeness.

### Survey design variables

The NHANES August 2021–August 2023 complex sampling design was accommodated by retaining the survey sampling weights, masked variance strata and primary sampling unit identifiers. The two-year phlebotomy sampling weight (WTPH2YR) was selected because the study required laboratory measurements obtained from blood specimens (serum creatinine and HbA1c). The masked stratum (SDMVSTRA) and primary sampling unit (SDMVPSU) variables were retained for subsequent survey-weighted analyses.


```{r survey-design-check}
survey_vars <- c("WTPH2YR", "SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU")

survey_check <- tibble(
  Variable = survey_vars,
  Present_in_ARD = survey_vars %in% names(ard)
)

knitr::kable(
  survey_check,
  caption = "Availability of NHANES survey design variables"
)

if (all(survey_check$Present_in_ARD)) {
  eligible %>%
    summarise(
      Eligible_N = n(),
      Missing_weight = sum(is.na(WTPH2YR)),
      Nonpositive_weight = sum(!is.na(WTPH2YR) & WTPH2YR <= 0),
      Missing_stratum = sum(is.na(SDMVSTRA)),
      Missing_PSU = sum(is.na(SDMVPSU))
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = "Survey design variable completeness among eligible participants"
    )
}
```
No missing or non-positive values were identified among the 3,370 eligible participants.

### Analysis-ready dataset

The analysis-ready dataset was constructed by retaining the 3,370 participants who met all study eligibility criteria. It contains:

- the participant identifier and demographic characteristics,  
- the primary albuminuria outcome and candidate regression variables,  
- derived clinical and metabolic-risk indicators,  
- the original measurements and questionnaire responses used to construct those indicators, and  
- the NHANES survey design variables.

Participants were not excluded solely because of missing regression covariates. The dataset was checked for participant-level uniqueness, eligibility consistency, outcome completeness and availability of survey design variables, then saved in RDS format for subsequent analyses.

```{r analysis-ready-dataset}
ard_columns <- c(
  "SEQN", "RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR", "RIDRETH3",
  "URDACT", "elevated_acr", "LBXSCR", "egfr", "LBXGH",
  "BPXOSY1", "BPXOSY2", "BPXOSY3",
  "BPXODI1", "BPXODI2", "BPXODI3",
  "mean_sbp", "mean_dbp", "BMXBMI",
  "DIQ010", "DIQ050", "DIQ070",
  "BPQ020", "BPQ150",
  "SMQ020", "SMQ040", "smoking_status",
  "diabetes", "hypertension", "obesity", "metabolic_risk",
  "WTPH2YR", "SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(ard_columns, names(ard))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Required columns missing from ard: ",
       paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

ard_final <- ard %>%
  filter(eligible_study) %>%
  select(all_of(ard_columns))

stopifnot(
  nrow(ard_final) == 3370,
  !anyNA(ard_final$SEQN),
  !anyDuplicated(ard_final$SEQN),
  all(ard_final$RIDAGEYR >= 20),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$URDACT)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$LBXSCR)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$egfr) & ard_final$egfr >= 60),
  all(ard_final$metabolic_risk == 1),
  !anyNA(ard_final$elevated_acr),
  all(ard_final$elevated_acr == (ard_final$URDACT >= 30)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$WTPH2YR) & ard_final$WTPH2YR > 0),
  !anyNA(ard_final$SDMVSTRA),
  !anyNA(ard_final$SDMVPSU)
)

tibble(
  Participants = nrow(ard_final),
  Variables = ncol(ard_final),
  Unique_participants = n_distinct(ard_final$SEQN),
  Elevated_albuminuria = sum(ard_final$elevated_acr)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Final analysis-ready dataset summary")
```

```{r preview-ard}
ard_final %>%
  select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR, elevated_acr, egfr, mean_sbp, BMXBMI, smoking_status) %>%
  head(3) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Preview of the analysis-ready dataset (first 3 rows, selected columns)")

```

```{r export-ards}
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveRDS(ard_final, file = "data/processed/nhanes_albuminuria_ard.rds")

ard_reloaded <- readRDS("data/processed/nhanes_albuminuria_ard.rds")
stopifnot(identical(ard_final, ard_reloaded))
```
The final analysis-ready dataset contained 3,370 eligible participants and 33 variables, of whom 417 (12.4 %, unweighted) had elevated albuminuria.

### Analysis-ready dataset validation
```{r preserve-survey-source, include=FALSE}
survey_source <- ard
```

```{r ard-validation, echo=FALSE}
ard <- readRDS("data/processed/nhanes_albuminuria_ard.rds")

checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Participant identifiers complete and unique",
    "All participants aged ≥20 years",
    "ACR complete, finite and nonnegative",
    "Outcome complete and consistent with ACR ≥30 mg/g",
    "eGFR complete, finite and ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²",
    "All participants have confirmed metabolic risk",
    "Survey weights finite and positive",
    "Survey strata and PSU identifiers complete",
    "Dataset dimensions match the final export",
    "Event count matches the final export"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    !anyNA(ard$SEQN) && !anyDuplicated(ard$SEQN),
    all(is.finite(ard$RIDAGEYR) & ard$RIDAGEYR >= 20),
    all(is.finite(ard$URDACT) & ard$URDACT >= 0),
    !anyNA(ard$elevated_acr) &&
      all(ard$elevated_acr == (ard$URDACT >= 30)),
    all(is.finite(ard$egfr) & ard$egfr >= 60),
    !anyNA(ard$metabolic_risk) &&
      all(ard$metabolic_risk == 1),
    all(is.finite(ard$WTPH2YR) & ard$WTPH2YR > 0),
    !anyNA(ard[c("SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU")]),
    nrow(ard) == 3370 && ncol(ard) == 33,
    !anyNA(ard$elevated_acr) &&
      sum(ard$elevated_acr) == 417
  )
)

if (!all(checks$Passed)) {
  stop(
    "ARD validation failed: ",
    paste(checks$Check[which(is.na(checks$Passed) |
                               !checks$Passed)], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

checks$Result <- ifelse(checks$Passed, "PASS", "FAIL")

knitr::kable(
  checks[c("Check", "Result")],
  caption = "Validation of the exported analysis-ready dataset"
)
```

The exported analysis-ready dataset was reloaded and checked for complete and unique participant identifiers, age eligibility, valid ACR and eGFR values, outcome-threshold consistency, confirmed metabolic-risk eligibility, and complete survey-design fields with finite positive weights. All checks passed. The dataset contained **3,370** participants and **417** elevated-albuminuria events, matching the final construction output.

Variable definitions, derivation rules and missing-value conventions are provided in the accompanying metadata file:  
[`metadata/nhanes_albuminuria_ard_codebook.md`](metadata/nhanes_albuminuria_ard_codebook.md)  
([GitHub](https://github.com/maheration/HDS_M1_NHANES/blob/main/metadata/nhanes_albuminuria_ard_codebook.md)).

**Residual limitations**

The analysis-ready dataset has the following limitations that should be considered when interpreting results:

- Albuminuria was assessed from a single urine sample; persistent albuminuria cannot be confirmed.
- Diabetes is an operational study phenotype based on self-reported diagnosis, HbA1c and medication use rather than a full clinical diagnosis.
- Hypertension and obesity remain indeterminate for a small number of participants when source measurements were incomplete.
- Questionnaire nonresponse and skip patterns may leave uncertainty in phenotype classification.
- Blood-pressure means may be based on different numbers of readings across participants.
- Age is top-coded at 80 years in the NHANES public-use file.


## Methods: 

### Statistical analysis

Analyses accounted for the NHANES complex, multistage probability sampling design. The two-year phlebotomy weight (WTPH2YR) was used together with the masked variance strata (SDMVSTRA) and primary sampling units (SDMVPSU), because the study required blood laboratory measures. The eligible study population was analysed as a subpopulation of the phlebotomy-weighted survey sample. Continuous variables were summarised as survey-weighted means and standard deviations; categorical variables were summarised as survey-weighted percentages. Unweighted sample sizes are reported. Descriptive summaries used available observations for each variable. The prevalence of elevated albuminuria was estimated with a logit-transformed 95% confidence interval. Between-group comparisons used design-based *t*-tests for continuous variables and Rao–Scott adjusted Pearson’s χ² tests for categorical variables.
```{r survey-design}
library(survey)

# Retain participants with valid phlebotomy weights
survey_base <- survey_source %>%
  filter(is.finite(WTPH2YR), WTPH2YR > 0)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(survey_base$SDMVSTRA),
  !anyNA(survey_base$SDMVPSU),
  !anyNA(survey_base$eligible_study)
)

# Declare the design before selecting the study population
design_full <- svydesign(
  ids     = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata  = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTPH2YR,
  data    = survey_base,
  nest    = TRUE
)

# Select eligible participants within the survey design
design <- subset(design_full, eligible_study)

# Confirm the same participants and ordering as the final ARD
stopifnot(
  nrow(design$variables) == 3370,
  sum(design$variables$elevated_acr) == 417,
  all(as.numeric(design$variables$SEQN) == as.numeric(ard$SEQN))
)
```


## Results

### Prevalence of elevated albuminuria

```{r prevalence}
prev <- svyciprop(~elevated_acr, design, method = "logit", na.rm = TRUE)

prev_table <- data.frame(
  Prevalence = sprintf("%.1f%%", prev * 100),
  CI = sprintf("%.1f%% to %.1f%%", 
               confint(prev)[1] * 100, 
               confint(prev)[2] * 100)
)

names(prev_table) <- c("Prevalence", "95% CI")

knitr::kable(prev_table, 
             caption = "Survey-weighted prevalence of elevated albuminuria (ACR ≥ 30 mg/g)",
             align = "c")
```
### Participant characteristics

Participants with elevated albuminuria were older and had higher mean HbA1c and systolic blood pressure than those without elevated albuminuria (Table 1). The weighted prevalence of diabetes was substantially higher in the elevated albuminuria group (49.8% vs 16.9%, *p* < 0.001), as was hypertension prevalence (83.8% vs 75.0%, *p* = 0.030). Race/ethnicity and smoking distributions also differed between groups. There was little difference in sex distribution or mean BMI.

```{r table1}
library(gtsummary)

ard$elevated_acr_f <- factor(
  ard$elevated_acr,
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("ACR < 30 mg/g", "ACR ≥ 30 mg/g")
)

ard$sex_f <- factor(
  ard$RIAGENDR,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Male", "Female")
)

ard$race_f <- factor(
  ard$RIDRETH3,
  levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7),
  labels = c(
    "Mexican American", "Other Hispanic",
    "Non-Hispanic White", "Non-Hispanic Black",
    "Non-Hispanic Asian", "Other/Multi"
  )
)

ard$diabetes_f <- factor(
  ard$diabetes, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

ard$hypertension_f <- factor(
  ard$hypertension, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

ard$obesity_f <- factor(
  ard$obesity, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

design <- update(
  design,
  elevated_acr_f = ard$elevated_acr_f,
  sex_f = ard$sex_f,
  race_f = ard$race_f,
  diabetes_f = ard$diabetes_f,
  hypertension_f = ard$hypertension_f,
  obesity_f = ard$obesity_f
)

tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = elevated_acr_f,
  include = c(
    RIDAGEYR, BMXBMI, LBXGH, mean_sbp, egfr,
    sex_f, race_f, smoking_status,
    diabetes_f, hypertension_f, obesity_f
  ),
  label = list(
    RIDAGEYR ~ "Age (years)",
    BMXBMI ~ "BMI (kg/m²)",
    LBXGH ~ "HbA1c (%)",
    mean_sbp ~ "Mean systolic BP (mmHg)",
    egfr ~ "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²)",
    sex_f ~ "Sex",
    race_f ~ "Race/ethnicity",
    smoking_status ~ "Smoking status",
    diabetes_f ~ "Diabetes",
    hypertension_f ~ "Hypertension",
    obesity_f ~ "Obesity"
  ),
  statistic = list(
    all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
    all_categorical() ~ "{p}%"
  ),
  digits = list(
    all_continuous() ~ 1,
    all_categorical() ~ 1
  ),
  missing = "no"
) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  add_p(
    test = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "svy.t.test",
      all_categorical() ~ "svy.chisq.test"
    )
  ) %>%
  modify_header(
    label = "**Characteristic**",
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**  \nN = {n_unweighted}"
  ) %>%
  modify_footnote_header(
    footnote = paste(
      "Unweighted sample sizes; survey-weighted means (SD) and percentages.",
      "For diabetes, hypertension and obesity, percentages represent participants with the condition."
      
    ),
    columns = all_stat_cols(),
    replace = TRUE
  ) %>%
  modify_footnote_header(
    footnote = paste(
      "Design-based t-test for continuous variables;",
      "Rao–Scott adjusted Pearson’s χ² test for categorical variables."
    ),
    columns = p.value,
    replace = TRUE
  ) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_caption(
    "**Table 1.** Participant characteristics by elevated albuminuria status"
  )
```
